ticket.summary: Active water pouring through dining room ceiling light fixture at 31 Halcyon Ct, likely from corroded upstairs toilet supply line; customer shut house main in garage and flow stopped — on-call dispatched.
mitigation_advice: Keep everyone out of the dining room, away from the sagging water-logged ceiling, and do not operate the affected light fixture [PB-08]
Shut off the house main (found next to water heater in garage) — turned clockwise, flow stopped [PB-02]
Attempt fixture-level shutoff on suspect upstairs toilet supply line (oval handle, clockwise) [PB-01]
Open the lowest cold tap in the house to drain remaining pressure from the lines [PB-03]

quote_lines.description: After-hours emergency dispatch surcharge; repair quoted after technician assessment

ticket.customer_message: Perfect — that's the main, great find. Leave it off. Now open the lowest cold tap in the house (basement sink or outdoor spigot) to bleed the remaining pressure — that's what the dripping is, and it'll ease off [PB-03]. Keep the dining room clear and that light off [PB-08]. The corroded toilet supply is a very likely culprit — don't touch it, just leave the toilet unused and let the tech confirm. Our on-call plumber is dispatched to 31 Halcyon Ct now and will call you when he's close. After-hours dispatch is $150; the repair itself gets quoted once he's seen it. Text back if anything changes before he arrives.
